summary:
Radar for 2026-10-25, GLP-1 focus. Best new opening: retatrutide and the kidneys (TRANSCEND-CKD). This Phase 2b trial was presented at ASN Kidney Week 2026, and HCPLive reported it on Oct 22. In adults with obesity or overweight and chronic kidney disease, retatrutide lowered albumin in the urine by 49.2% versus placebo at 24 weeks. Measured kidney filtration (GFR) did not change. It is a new retatrutide result with almost no consumer explainers yet, which is the EloraTZP pattern (Lane C / pipeline lane). It is about 3 days old, so it sits just outside the strict 48-hour Lane C window. Run it as the 'new drug decoded' long-form with a 20:00 funnel Short.

Next opening: petrelintide, an amylin drug. Medical News Today ran it on Oct 24. Up to 10.7% weight loss at 42 weeks, and only 1.5% stopped because of stomach side effects. It's an under-covered name, good for the weekly 'What Is [new drug]?' test. Third: CagriSema in women. A REDEFINE 1 post hoc analysis (Oct 22) found 25.0% average loss versus 3.0% on placebo, including results by menopause stage. It pairs with the Mayo semaglutide-plus-hormone-therapy cohort.

Retatrutide Shorts are still hot. Futurism's Oct 24 lab test of 'bodega' retatrutide and the South African 'Reta' coverage (Oct 22–25) feed a 'what's confirmed?' Short, and the NEJM sleep apnea results are still getting pickup (Medical Xpress, Oct 24). Hanmi's efpeglenatide launches in Korea on Oct 29, which gives a pipeline explainer a dated hook.

Lane A long-forms with real search demand and a fresh hook:
- Tirzepatide side effects, hooked to The Conversation's Oct 22 nausea piece and a Diabetes Obes Metab review on how trials measure nausea.
- What happens when you stop.
- Medicare GLP-1 coverage during open enrollment (Oct 15–Dec 7).
- Thanksgiving on GLP-1, peaking about Nov 18–27.
- Why GLP-1s work better for some people (genetics).

Checked and dropped as not new: the Wegovy 'eye stroke' story (an FAERS analysis from March 2026) and Lilly's Zepbound price cut (an older story). Rejected: microdosing articles (Yahoo Oct 24, India Today Oct 25). I could not open the abstract of the new bone systematic review (Arch Osteoporos, Oct 23), so the fact-checker must confirm it before any claim is made.

candidates.topic: Retatrutide and the kidneys: TRANSCEND-CKD Phase 2b (ASN Kidney Week 2026) in adults with obesity or overweight and chronic kidney disease, with or without type 2 diabetes: urine albumin down 49.2% versus placebo at 24 weeks, plus lower pressure inside the kidney's filters and less kidney fat, with no change in measured GFR
candidates.angle: New GLP-1 Drug Decoded (Lane C / pipeline). Title: 'Retatrutide and Your Kidneys: What the New Trial Found'. Explain in plain words what albuminuria and pressure inside the kidney's filters mean. Say clearly that this is a 24-week mechanism study, not an outcomes trial. TRIUMPH-Outcomes (about 5 years) will test kidney and heart events. Retatrutide is investigational and not approved. Tie it back to the approved evidence: semaglutide in FLOW (type 2 diabetes with chronic kidney disease). Funnel Short at 20:00.
candidates.predicted_peak: 3–10 days (more pickup in medical press after Kidney Week, then consumer)
candidates.why_now: Presented at ASN Kidney Week 2026 (Denver). HCPLive story Oct 22. The name 'retatrutide' gets our highest Short peaks (253, 196), and almost no consumer channel has explained the kidney data. Kidney is a supported 'beyond weight' pillar.

evidence.signal: TRANSCEND-CKD 24-week data: UACR −49.2% vs placebo, lower intraglomerular pressure and kidney fat, measured GFR unchanged
Trial design: Phase 2b, obesity or overweight with chronic kidney disease, with or without type 2 diabetes; primary endpoint measured GFR (iohexol) at week 24
Conference record of the presentation
Ongoing heart and kidney outcomes trial, so the outcome answer is still pending

candidates.topic: What is petrelintide? Zealand and Roche's amylin drug: up to 10.7% weight loss at 42 weeks in ZUPREME-1, stomach side effects mostly mild (nausea 20% vs 6% placebo), 1.5% stopped because of stomach side effects
candidates.angle: 'What Is Petrelintide? The Amylin Drug Built for Fewer Side Effects'. Explain how amylin differs from GLP-1 (fullness, slower stomach emptying) and why companies are pairing it with GLP-1 drugs. It's Phase 2 and investigational. Show the honest trade-off: less weight loss than tirzepatide so far, but gentler on the stomach. No 'beat' frame.
keywords: new weight loss drug fewer side effects
candidates.why_now: Medical News Today ran it on Oct 24 ('may have fewer GI effects than GLP-1s'), following Healio, Pharmacy Times and HCPLive in early October. The name is under-covered and has published human data, which is exactly the weekly pipeline-explainer test in the playbook.

evidence.source: Medical News Today via Google News (Oct 24, 2026)
evidence.signal: Mainstream consumer pickup, early stage
ZUPREME-1: up to 10.7% weight loss at 42 weeks, mostly mild stomach side effects
ZUPREME-2 in type 2 diabetes with obesity beat placebo; 1.9% vs 1.7% stopped because of stomach side effects
About 10% weight loss with adverse events comparable to placebo

candidates.topic: CagriSema in women: REDEFINE 1 post hoc found 25.0% average weight loss versus 3.0% on placebo at 68 weeks (2,309 women with obesity or overweight), with similar results before, during and after menopause (26.7%, 24.8%, 23.1%)
candidates.angle: Search-question long-form: 'Do GLP-1 Medicines Work After Menopause?' Combine the CagriSema post hoc (investigational, not approved) with the retrospective Mayo cohort on semaglutide plus hormone therapy (linked to more loss, observational). Say clearly what a post hoc analysis can and can't show, and give nausea (55%), constipation and vomiting rates. Women 45–65 are a core high-ad-rate audience.
candidates.why_now: Pharmacy Times (Oct 22) and pharmaphorum covered the post hoc, AARP ran '5 menopause research updates' (Oct 23), and Patient Care covered the Mayo hormone-therapy cohort (Oct 23). Three independent sources in 3 days, and menopause plus GLP-1 is a heavily searched question.

evidence.signal: CagriSema 25% weight loss in women, post hoc of REDEFINE 1
'CagriSema Tied to 25% Weight Loss in Women, Post Hoc Data Show'

evidence.source: Patient Care Online via Google News (Oct 23, 2026)
evidence.signal: Menopause hormone therapy linked to greater weight loss with semaglutide (real-world)
Company statement of the post hoc results

candidates.topic: What did lab tests find in 'retatrutide' sold online and in shops? Futurism's chemical analysis of 'bodega' retatrutide (Oct 24), The Sun's experts on fake 'Reta' jabs (Oct 22), and the South African black market (News24 Oct 25, Mail & Guardian Oct 22)
candidates.angle: Gray-market 'what's confirmed?' Short (13:00 lead slot), phrased as a question: 'Is That Retatrutide Real? What Lab Tests Found'. Credit every line to the outlet that published it, with the date. State that retatrutide is not approved anywhere and that Lilly doesn't sell it, then point viewers to a prescriber about approved options or clinical trials. Name no sellers. Keep it a Short; gray-market long-forms are paused.
candidates.why_now: A second wave after CBS's Oct 21 lab tests: Futurism (Oct 24), The Sun (Oct 22), UNILAD (Oct 22), News24 (Oct 25). Retatrutide gray-market Shorts are among our best (196).

evidence.signal: 'Someone Ran a Chemical Analysis of Bodega Retatrutide'
Experts warn fake 'Reta' jabs could increase appetite and worsen sleep
South Africans injecting illicit 'Reta'

candidates.topic: Retatrutide for sleep apnea: TRIUMPH-1-OSA (243 adults, no diabetes) and TRIUMPH-2-OSA (448 adults, type 2 diabetes), BMI 27 or higher, published in NEJM, with fresh pickup from Medical Xpress (Oct 24) and Physicians Weekly (Oct 23)
candidates.angle: Two-drug head-to-head Short with tirzepatide named first: 'Tirzepatide vs Retatrutide for Sleep Apnea: Approved vs Investigational'. Label it an indirect comparison (SURMOUNT-OSA vs TRIUMPH-OSA) with a dated status and each drug's common side effects. If no retatrutide sleep apnea long-form is live yet, make one: 'Retatrutide for Sleep Apnea: What the New Trials Found'.
candidates.why_now: Seen in 4+ snapshots with momentum around 86–91, and consumer science press is still picking it up 4 days after NEJM. Coverage is broadening rather than fading.

evidence.signal: 'Triple-action weekly weight-loss drug reduces sleep apnea in two late-stage trials'
Retatrutide cuts sleep apnea severity with and without type 2 diabetes
Review of tirzepatide for sleep apnea, the approved comparator

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide side effects: which are common and what helps. Hooked to The Conversation's 'nausea needs closer study' (Oct 22), the Diabetes Obes Metab review of how trials measure nausea (Oct 22) and the Neurogastroenterol Motil review of stomach symptoms and gut motility
candidates.angle: Lane A long-form: 'Tirzepatide Side Effects: Which Are Common and What Helps'. Use the trial rates by dose, explain why nausea is mostly early and dose-related, and give practical, non-dosing tips (smaller meals, stop at full, hydration, lower-fat meals). Give the label's 'call your provider right away' warning signs word for word. New fact: trials may under-measure how nausea feels day to day.
keywords: how to stop nausea on Mounjaro
candidates.predicted_peak: evergreen; steady search with a fresh hook this week
candidates.why_now: Seen in 10 snapshots with steady momentum, now refreshed by The Conversation and a new review the same week. It's a top tirzepatide search question, and tirzepatide-named titles are our proven Shorts lever.

evidence.signal: GLP-1 drugs change how people eat, but nausea needs closer study
Narrative review: gaps in how GLP-1 obesity trials measure nausea from the patient's side
Stomach symptoms and motility changes with GLP-1 medicines

candidates.topic: Does Medicare cover Wegovy or Zepbound? The Medicare GLP-1 Bridge's $50-a-month copay (Jul 1, 2026 to Dec 31, 2027) and who qualifies, during open enrollment (Oct 15 to Dec 7)
candidates.angle: Lane A long-form: 'Does Medicare Cover Zepbound or Wegovy? Who Qualifies'. Quote CMS eligibility word for word with dates, cover every eligibility pathway, add 'if you qualify', and give questions to bring to your doctor and plan. No pricing hacks and no online sources.
candidates.why_now: Local TV (FOX 48, Oct 24) is explaining who qualifies, and open enrollment creates a 6-week window of searches from older US adults with high ad value.

evidence.signal: 'Who qualifies for Medicare's new $50-a-month GLP-1 program?'

candidates.topic: What happens when you stop semaglutide or tirzepatide? SURMOUNT-4 and the STEP 1 extension on regain, plus the new US real-world study on early stopping and 1-year persistence with semaglutide (Diabetes Obes Metab, Oct 19)
candidates.angle: Lane A long-form: 'What Happens When You Stop Tirzepatide or Semaglutide?' Explain what regain looks like in the trials, what helped people keep results (strength training, protein, follow-up), and why most people stop early in real life. Never give stopping advice; this is a 'talk to your prescriber' topic.
keywords: what happens when you stop Ozempic
candidates.why_now: Seen in 11 snapshots, with a fresh real-world persistence paper this month and Medscape's 'not a quick fix' piece (Oct 22). It's a durable top search question.

evidence.signal: Real-world semaglutide starting patterns, early stopping and 1-year persistence in the US
'Beyond the Scale: Weight-Loss Drugs Aren't a Quick Fix'

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide: how much of the weight lost is muscle? SURMOUNT-1 body-scan substudy, the semaglutide handgrip-strength meta-analysis (Oct 19), and new muscle-sparing add-on drugs in trials (trevogrumab, apitegromab; Earth.com Oct 24)
candidates.angle: Outcome-question Short (08:00): 'Tirzepatide: How Much of the Weight Lost Is Muscle?' Lead with the body-scan share, then handgrip strength, then what keeps muscle (protein, resistance training). Mention the add-on drugs only as 'in trials'. Run a funnel spin-off to the live Strength Training on Tirzepatide long-form.
keywords: how to keep muscle on tirzepatide
candidates.why_now: Earth.com (Oct 24) is reviving the 'muscle loss' story, and muscle outcome questions have scored 131 and 101 for us. The Strength Training long-form (40) is live and ready to receive funnel traffic.

evidence.signal: Systematic review and meta-analysis of handgrip strength on semaglutide
'New therapy may prevent muscle loss from weight-loss drugs'

candidates.topic: Thanksgiving and holiday meals on tirzepatide or semaglutide: protein first, smaller plates, eating slower, and easing nausea and fullness at big meals
candidates.angle: Lane A 'Life on GLP-1' long-form, published about Nov 10–17 to rank before the peak: 'Thanksgiving on Tirzepatide: What to Eat and What Helps'. Encouraging and non-restrictive: enjoying food, protein-first plates, alcohol and nausea, no extreme diet messaging. Follow with a Short the week of Nov 23.
candidates.why_now: A seasonal cycle about to start. Seen in 8+ snapshots, and UC Davis Health already published a guide (Oct 20). Searches build through November.

evidence.signal: Supports the mechanism behind slower stomach emptying and fullness, for the eating-slower tips
Obesity doctor on getting the best results on GLP-1s (lifestyle demand)

candidates.topic: What is efpeglenatide? Hanmi's weekly GLP-1, approved in Korea and launching about Oct 29: Phase 3 in 448 adults with obesity without diabetes, 9.02% versus 0.89% placebo at 40 weeks, with lower nausea and vomiting
candidates.angle: Pipeline explainer timed to the launch (a dated regulatory step): 'Efpeglenatide: The New Weekly GLP-1 Explained'. Explain why it matters (price, tolerability), where it's approved (Korea only, with the date), and that it isn't available in the US, UK, Canada or Australia. No 'beat' frame. Calm, honest comparison of trial numbers, labelled indirect.
candidates.why_now: Korea Biomedical Review and Yonhap report an Oct 29 launch. It's a brand-new name for Western audiences, with almost no English explainer videos (the EloraTZP pattern), although audience fit is lower because it isn't approved locally.

evidence.source: Korea Biomedical Review via Google News (Oct 23, 2026)
evidence.signal: Hanmi's first Korean-developed GLP-1 obesity drug set for Oct 29 launch
Approval with less weight loss but fewer side effects

candidates.topic: Were Zepbound or Mounjaro recalled? No. The nationwide recall covers compounded GLP-1 injections over sterility concerns (BioPharma Dive 'copycat Zepbound' Oct 22, The Hill: 22 vials of tirzepatide and one of NAD+, FOX/WSB/Dallas News Oct 22–24)
candidates.angle: Gray-market 'what's confirmed?' Short, phrased as a question: 'Was Zepbound Recalled? What the FDA Notice Covers'. Quote the FDA enforcement record with the date, name the compounder only as the recall record does, and say Lilly's KwikPen and vials aren't part of it. Point viewers to a prescriber. Counts as this week's one recall Short.
candidates.why_now: Wall-to-wall local TV coverage (Oct 22–24) creates confused searches. The differentiated angle is 'what it is and isn't'.

evidence.signal: 'GLP-1 compounder issues recall for copycat Zepbound'

evidence.source: LiveNOW from FOX via Google News (Oct 24, 2026)
evidence.signal: FDA recalls GLP-1 injections over sterility concerns

candidates.topic: Wegovy pill versus Wegovy shot: oral semaglutide uptake nearly matched injectables within 3 months (AJMC, HealthDay, Medical Xpress Oct 22–23), plus the OCTANE switch study (4.1% further loss at 3 months, 194 adults, retrospective)
candidates.angle: Lane A long-form: 'Wegovy Pill vs Wegovy Shot: What's the Difference?' Cover how each is taken in general terms (no dosing), the trial results for each, side effects for each, and who might ask their doctor about which. Add 'don't switch on your own'. Searches like 'wegovy pill pros and cons' and 'how effective is the wegovy pill' are showing up.
keywords: how effective is the Wegovy pill
candidates.why_now: Several outlets ran the uptake study on Oct 22–23, and query-style headlines show what people are searching.

evidence.signal: Early uptake was rapid for oral semaglutide relative to injectables

evidence.source: Patient Care Online via Google News (Oct 22, 2026)
evidence.signal: Switching to oral semaglutide linked to 4.1% weight loss at 3 months

candidates.topic: Why do GLP-1 medicines work better for some people? Genetics, with a GLP1R gene variant linked to more weight loss (23andMe study in Nature, Apr 2026, 27,885 users), resurfaced by Yahoo Health on Oct 23
candidates.angle: Lane A long-form: 'Why Does Ozempic Work Better for Some People?' Cover the trial spread of responses, what predicts response (genes, diabetes status, sex, adherence), and why gene tests aren't a clinical tool yet. Positive message: not responding fast isn't failure, so talk to your prescriber. No promotion of gene-test products.
keywords: why isn't Ozempic working for me
why does semaglutide work better for some
candidates.predicted_peak: evergreen with a 1–2 week news lift
candidates.why_now: A Yahoo Health pickup (Oct 23) makes a strong evergreen search question topical again. The underlying study is solid but observational.

evidence.signal: 'Your Genes May Predict How Your Body Reacts To GLP-1s'
Summary of the genetic-markers GWAS (27,885 GLP-1 users)

candidates.topic: Do 'GLP-1 supplements' work like semaglutide? Fortune's 'best GLP-1 boosters' (Oct 22), Reuters and Japan Today (Oct 23) on doctors and regulators raising flags, plus berberine, fibre, probiotics, drops and patches
candidates.angle: Myth-correction long-form or Short: 'Do GLP-1 Supplements Work? What the Evidence Says'. Show how small the human data on supplements are compared with the drug trials, explain natural ways to support your own GLP-1 (protein, fibre, eating order) without claiming they replace the medicine, and cover FDA warning letters. Name no products.
candidates.why_now: Three outlets in 3 days, with TikTok-driven demand. A myth-correction pillar with strong search volume.

evidence.signal: 'The Best GLP-1 Boosters and Supplements (2026)'
Doctors and regulators raise flags as weight-loss drug users turn to supplements

candidates.topic: Do GLP-1 medicines affect your bones? New systematic review of skeletal effects in adults with overweight or obesity (Arch Osteoporos, Oct 23, 2026)
candidates.angle: 'Honest uncertainty' body-worry Short (eye, pancreas, gallbladder, hair, now bones): 'Semaglutide and Your Bones: What This Review Can't Say'. Cover bone density versus fractures, whether bone loss is weight-loss-related, and the value of strength training and protein. The fact-checker must read the full abstract first; I could not open it.
candidates.why_now: A fresh systematic review that no creators have covered yet. This format got 104 on YouTube and 160 on Instagram (macular degeneration), and bone worries are common in women over 50.

evidence.signal: Systematic review: skeletal effects of GLP-1 receptor agonists in adults with overweight or obesity

candidates.topic: Does semaglutide help people drink less? Medical Economics (Oct 23) 'semaglutide cuts heavy drinking', the Addictive Behaviors review, and STAT (Oct 22) on telehealth off-label prescribing for addiction
candidates.angle: 'Promising early research' long-form: 'Does Semaglutide Reduce Alcohol Cravings? What Trials Show'. Cover the small randomized trials, the brain-reward mechanism, and the fact that it isn't approved for alcohol use disorder. Point viewers to a clinician and evidence-based alcohol support. Never explain how to get it off-label.
candidates.why_now: Repeated mentions across snapshots, with new trade-press coverage, and cutting back on alcohol becomes a common goal before the holidays.

evidence.signal: 'semaglutide cuts heavy drinking' in the morning update
Telehealth off-label GLP-1 prescriptions for addiction ahead of FDA approval

candidates.angle: Head-to-head Short with both drugs named and 'indirect' in the title: 'Orforglipron vs Semaglutide Pill: An Indirect Comparison'. Give the dated EU status (CHMP opinion Oct 16, Commission decision pending) and side effects for each. Lower priority, because orforglipron Shorts have scored 36–39.
candidates.why_now: A fresh comparison story on pills, a format with search interest. Not a randomized head-to-head, so 'beat' framing is banned.

candidates.angle: Do not cover. Microdosing and self-titration protocols are banned for this channel. If viewers ask, the only allowed response is a general line: dose decisions belong to your prescriber.
